memory_candidates.content: Bash lint-script gotcha under `set -euo pipefail`: a helper function that signals outcomes via `return 1`/`return 2` (e.g. a section locator with a 'not found' vs. 'decided skip' distinction) must NEVER be called as `var=$(helper_fn); status=$?` directly -- under `set -e`, a failing command substitution in a plain assignment trips the shell's exit-on-error even though it 'looks like' status is being checked afterward. Always call it inside an `if`/`while`/`||` test (`if helper_fn ...; then ... else status=$?; ... fi`), which bash explicitly exempts from `set -e`. Pass multi-value results back via global variables set inside the function rather than via stdout+command-substitution when the function's own return code also needs to be tested, since you cannot cleanly capture both stdout AND a safely-tested exit code from one `var=$(fn)` call under `set -e`.

When verify-deploy.sh (or any whole-repo gate) shows a failure during a live multi-task /orchestrate batch, before treating it as a regression from your own dispatch: check `git status --porcelain` and `git log --oneline -1` on the implicated file(s). If the file is (a) outside your own task's declared file_scope, (b) currently uncommitted, and (c) last committed by an unrelated prior task, it is very likely a concurrently-dispatched sibling's in-flight edit, not your regression -- a content-hash mismatch in particular can self-resolve on a bare retry once the sibling commits. Record it as a Reasoned Exclusion (status-markers.md's [COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS] admission test) with the git evidence inline, rather than chasing a moving target or silently reporting a false green.
